scope: Corollary 9.5 of the manuscript “Algebraic Kuga–Satake correspondences and Hodge conjectures on a K3 quadratic locus” (preprints/Algebraic-Kuga-Satake-correspondences-and-Hodge-conjectures-on-a-K3-quadratic-locus-September-30-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 032 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c9fde2b758f25505), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 61. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let S be a smooth projective complex K3 surface admitting a rational isometric embedding (TS, q) ,→ VP . For every n, r ≥ 1, rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of (S[n])r, where S[n] is the Hilbert scheme of length-n subschemes of S. More generally, let α ∈ Br(S) and let M be either a smooth projective moduli space of Gieseker- stable α-twisted sheaves on S, or a smooth projective moduli space of σ-stable objects in Db(S, α) for a generic Bridgeland stability condition σ. Then rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of Mr for every r ≥ 1. If M is hyperkähler, the same conclusions hold for every smooth projective hyperkähler variety birational to M and all its self-powers.
